Afternoon in a cramped chikankari tailor shop in Aminabad, Lucknow, two hours before a wedding. Master Haroon (60s), a proud tailor, fits Pramod (30s), the groom's cousin, in a sherwani that is visibly too tight. Pramod gasps that he cannot breathe; Haroon insists the cut is flawless and it is Pramod who is wrong, and tells him to stop breathing so much. Pramod holds his breath and stands very straight while Haroon pins the hem with great dignity. A button pings off the chest, flies across the shop and lands in Haroon's tea glass. They both stare at it; Haroon fishes it out, dries it on his sleeve, and says it is a sign the garment is alive.
